# Independent audit: concave-array parameter compactness

Audited source: `candidate 27d482de82ed9f88`, Sections 1–6. Verdict: PASS. No repair is required. The original bad-sublevel body compactness and original closed-minor theorem remain explicit dependencies; they are not reproved by the parameter argument.

## 1. Finite roofs and normalization

The extreme anchored representations are finite and have affinely independent supports. They therefore define a closed polyhedral sampled-concavity cone. The maximum barycentric interpolation is concave by mixing representations and reproduces every sample precisely by the defining anchored inequalities. It is the least concave extension, is continuous on the entire base polytope, and has the stated uniform sup-norm stability. Boundary bases introduce no interpolation discontinuity.

The energy-root/geometric-mean composition is jointly concave with the exact exponents d/(d+1) and 1/(d+1). Its continuous derivative is f times the projective normalizer. Neither assertion requires differentiability of the base roof. The finite array normalization is unaffected by continuous affine normalization of the actual fibers.

## 2. The new arithmetic step

The positive set U of a nonnegative sampled-concave array has the following precise closure property: the integer midpoint of a positive point and any other sampled point remains positive whenever the midpoint is integral. This is the only additional property used by the maximal-threshold proof. In particular the zero set need not be a closed minor, convex, or contained in one face.

At a coordinatewise maximal feasible threshold vector, every nonsaturated cap has an exclusive equality witness in U. The surviving strict trace T is a closed minor: each defining strict affine inequality remains strict on the convex hull of its finitely many points. Witness–witness and witness–survivor midpoint contradictions prove r+k(T)<=k. The covering caps still have strictly smaller mass than M/k, so their union gives the strict mass contradiction. T is proper because the nonempty positive set has been excluded. The empty-T case is handled separately. All atoms on selected cap boundaries remain on the closed side throughout.

Consequently the new statement is a valid extension of the complement-face lemma. No unsupported subtraction of the parities of the entire zero and positive sets occurs.

## 3. Escape and fixed-epsilon attainment

Dividing a normalized multiplier array by its weighted arithmetic mean produces uniformly bounded positive arrays with weighted mean one. Their limits are nonnegative sampled-concave and nonzero. If every limiting coordinate is positive, the exact geometric-normalization identity restores a finite positive limit. Otherwise the geometric denominator tends to zero, despite varying weights: one logarithm tends to minus infinity with a uniformly positive coefficient and every other logarithm is bounded above. Every positive limiting coordinate consequently has multiplier tending to infinity.

The arithmetic lemma selects one such positive base whose LIMITING atomic depth is at least 1/k. At that fixed base, the actual fiber centroid has energy equal to its positive volume. Uniform covariance positivity and bounded fiber radius then make the buffered caps capture all fibers with nonnegative base drift, uniformly over every continuous unit normal and every base tilt. The depth at that mark equals atomic depth. Finite atomic traces make that depth continuous in the finite weight vector. Thus escape contradicts a bad sublevel b<Gamma_d/k<1/k.

Once the arrays have finite positive limits, their roof convergence and the existing positive-fiber, all-direction slab estimate give joint buffered-depth continuity. This proves the claimed attained infimum at each fixed epsilon for which a strict bad reference pair exists. No limiting derivative or quantitative rate in epsilon is used.

The minimum-value comparison with the constant array is valid because E<=V and the covariance norm is uniformly bounded in the normalized compact body family. It provides convergence of minimum VALUES only. The source correctly does not claim multiplier bounds uniform as epsilon tends to zero, own-properness at the new optimizers, or a response payment.

## 4. Verification and scope

Independently read and reran `supporting computation verify_concave_array_geometric_attainment_two_sided.py`: PASS, 466 exact checks, including 89 proper closed minors. These finite checks verify roof/normalization and the non-face zero-set calibration; the compactness theorem is justified by the analytic proof above, not the enumeration.

This enlargement supplies additional legal parameter directions at a genuinely attained unpenalized extremum. Equality in the additional sampled concavity inequalities must still be tracked where old affine-multiplier rigidity is used. In the specific mixed-status argument, that equality follows exactly, as shown next.

## 5. Mixed-status heredity extends, with a tight multiplier contact

Fix any positive sampled-concave multiplier, its canonical roof, and epsilon>0. Let I be the actual buffered deepest bases, J those with atomic base depth strictly greater than the common deepest value Q, and A=I outside J. Take a positive anchored representation r=sum_j lambda_j p_j with r in J and all p_j in I. Choose deepest marks y_j and form y=sum_j lambda_j y_j. The joint buffered level region makes (r,y) deepest.

The proper active cap at (r,y) is attained and has exact upper quantile c_Q, as in the audited mixed-status source. Applying its quantile inequalities to all input deepest marks forces

    f(r,y)=sum_j lambda_j f(p_j,y_j).

Put F_j=E_(K_pj)(y_j)^(1/d), F_r=E_(K_r)(y)^(1/d), and

    G(s,t)=s^(d/(d+1)) t^(1/(d+1)).

After removing the common positive factor M^(-1/(d+1)), the equality above is the equality case of the chain

    G(F_r,ell_r)
      >=G(sum_j lambda_j F_j, sum_j lambda_j ell_j)
      >=sum_j lambda_j G(F_j,ell_j).

All arguments are strictly positive. Joint energy concavity and sampled multiplier concavity give the first inequality coordinatewise. Strict monotonicity of G therefore forces BOTH

    F_r=sum_j lambda_j F_j,
    ell_r=sum_j lambda_j ell_j.

Equality in weighted geometric-mean concavity gives F_j/ell_j constant. The existing joint-energy equality theorem then gives the exact marked homotheties of whole fibers, K_pj-y_j=ell_j K_*, including the exact target fiber K_r-y=ell_r K_*. Also f(p_j,y_j)/ell_j is common.

The same active cap consequently has identical normalized own-fiber traces at every input and at r. It is proper at r. An atomic input would have every own buffered trace full, a contradiction. Thus every positive input lies in J. This proves the old hereditary statement for positive concave arrays, and additionally identifies a tight sampled-multiplier contact on every such representation.

The remaining arithmetic argument uses only this heredity, convexity of the buffered deepest region and actual atomic caps. It therefore carries over unchanged: J and A are closed minors, and the compressed atomic caps have m exclusive witnesses with

    m+k(J)<=k(I).

This is a relation-by-relation conclusion. It does not make ell globally affine, and it supplies no continuous-cap payment for mass outside I. It also does not transfer any parameter stationarity formula whose admissible directions were specifically the affine subspace.
note: Mathematical discussion retained to expose corrections and limitations. This is not a verification run, accepted premise, or approval of the revised submission. Association follows explicit source-document references, not an inferred dependency.
